title: Cellular Senescence and Senotherapies in the Kidney
abstract:
Calcitriol, an active form of vitamin D, has anti-proliferative activity against a number of cancers including renal cancer.
*In vitro* studies have attributed this effect to calcitriol inducing senescence with increased expression of P16^INK4A^ (Shen et al., 2017).
...
An association between cellular senescence and resultant fibrosis has also been shown in the liver, where transgenic induction of senescence significantly exaggerates fibrosis in the context of acute injury.
(Ferreira-Gonzalez et al., 2018) Similarly, in the kidney, transgenic depletion of SCs in the INK-ATTAC model resulted in significantly less glomerulosclerosis (Baker et al., 2016).
